stemMd: The final reference to a policy's “exclusions” refers most directly to

options.label: A
options.textMd: population variation and collection circumstances not represented in the stored sample.

options.label: B
options.textMd: rules forbidding researchers from reading records.

options.label: C
options.textMd: the financial cost of insuring a storage building.

options.label: D
options.textMd: all species that cannot be grown indoors.

options.label: E
options.textMd: legal restrictions on entering every collection site.

explanationMd: Read the metaphor through the argument it summarizes. The collection insures against loss only to the extent of what it contains. Its exclusions are its sampling gaps and limitations, which records make visible.

distractorRationale.c: The insurance language is an analogy for biological protection.
distractorRationale.e: Access limits are only one possible cause, not the metaphor's full referent.
